recipes.name: Sangria Ham
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 pound) bone-in ham with rind removed

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Use a sharp knife to score the ham 1/4 inch deep in a diamond pattern. Place in a good sized roaster with the fat side up, and stud in a decorative manner with the whole cloves...be sure to use plenty. Pack the top of the ham with the whole pound of brown sugar to coat the surface as thickly as possible. Some may fall off into the pan, but that can not be helped. Leave it there to sweeten the basting juices needed in later steps.

Roast, uncovered, until the sugar begins to melt, about 20 minutes. During this time, mix together the pineapple juice and sangria. When the sugar has begun to melt, pour one cup of the wine mixture over the ham, and return the ham to the oven for 40 minutes. I often tent the ham with foil at some point, but my mother never did.

After one hour in the oven, baste the ham with a second cup of the wine mixture, stirring it into the pan drippings. Return the ham to the oven for 2 more hours, basting after the first hour with the remaining wine mixture.

Lower the oven temperature to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C), and baste the ham every 20 minutes with the pan drippings for the final hour of cooking. A meat thermometer should read 160 degrees F (65 degrees C) before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Sangria Ham
raw_recipe.description: Allow half a day to roast this bone-in ham studded with whole cloves and basted in a red wine and pineapple juice punch.

review.reviewBody: Fantastic! As pork producers, we always have a freezer full of pork and I'm always looking for new ways to cook it. This recipe was the best! I did make a couple of minor changes. I cooked a cured ham coated in brown sugar in the oven for the first twenty minutes, then I transferred it to the slow cooker. I used a merlot I had on hand instead of the sangria and added all the liquid to the slowcooker at once, basting the ham every hour or so. When the ham was cooked, I transferred it back to the roaster and strained the remaining liquid into a saucepan. I thickened the liquid on the stovetop with a little cornstarch. This made a lovely burgundy sauce which I used to glaze the ham before I placed it under the broiler for five minutes to make the top shiny and just a little crisp. I served the remaining sauce with the ham.

This is delicious!! I've made all kinds of glazes and sauces for ham for 30 years + and this is the best. My search is over. I used a honey baked spiral sliced ham. I put the ham (without cloves), juice and sangria in the crockpot then packed the brown sugar on the ham. Then I went out to the pool. I turned the ham over and basted a couple of times. It was cooked in 4 hours but the longer the better. So easy and tasty! Serve with Pineapple Stuffing and Stewed Tomatoes.

AMAZING!!! Used a whole boneless hickory smoked pit ham -13.5 lbs. I added the wine mixture to the pan within about 10 minutes when the brown sugar smelled like it was melting. I also turned the oven down to 325 after the first 20 minutes so that it wouldn’t burn. Doubled the juice/wine mixture. It thickened without cooking on stovetop. The glaze is deep, rich and delicious! Best ham ever!!!

Made this for the first time for Thanksgiving today and it was a HUGE hit. Absolutely a GREAT ham recipe. I only tweaked the recipe slightly. Instead of straight pineapple juice, I pureed a can of crushed pineapple and used a cup of that. I went just slightly light on the quantity of brown sugar and added a 1/2 cup of pure maple syrup (the good stuff, don't cheep out) to the sangria/pineapple puree mix. I used a 7lb pre-cooked store-bought ham and followed the baking instructions supplied with the ham I bought which cut the oven time down to 2 hours at 325 degrees. After the first 30 minutes, I ladled the juices over the top every 15 minutes for the duration of time. As other reviews suggested I then reduced the drippings, added a little corn starch to thicken and served on the side. Everybody loved it! Thanks for a great recipe!

Simply amazing ham! To make it healthier, I replace the unsweetened pineapple juice with pineapple chunks pureed in a blender until it liquifies. This eliminates a lot of sugar and preservatives from the canned juice. I also cut down on the amount of brown sugar and replace some of it with apple sauce which has natural sweetening ability. I make my own sangria; that way I can control the ingredients in the sangria by adding or taking out anything I want. I also added some minced Vidalia onion to the brown sugar and it was excellent.

Everyone in my extended family loved this! It was my first time cooking a ham,and it was equally simple and delicious. I followed other reviewers and baked it in the oven for 20-30 minutes with the brown sugar packed on. Then I put it in my crockpot on low for 6 hours. I used an 8 lb pre-cooked spiral ham and I had doubled the juice and wine, as I like a lot of sauce. It turns out that even though the liquid covered 80% of the ham, it was moist, but seemed a bit overcooked. I will definitely do this again, but if you are going to use a precooked ham I STRONGLY suggest that you cook it for less time so it doesn't dry out. Also, I used a cornstarch slurry to thicken up the juice into sauce and it was raved over. THANKS for the only ham recipe I'll ever need!

Absolutely phenomenal recipe! I made this for my husbands work luncheon and it was gone in minutes. I omitted the cloves but followed the other recipe ingredients exactly. We did used a precooked ham because that was provided to us. Baked at 400 for 20 ish minutes until all the brown sugar was melting and then reduced down to 275 for 1.5 hours per the packaging recommendations. Made a reduction with the juice in the pan by adding some corn starch and boiling until thickened. I can't recommend this one enough, you won't be disappointed.

Wow! I made this for my family's Christmas Dinner and it was amazingly good. Great rich flavor without being too sweet and the glaze really balanced the saltiness of the ham just right. I used Chianti for the wine and recommend it. Chianti is the tradition wine for Sangria and has a very fruity flavor itself. I used the pineapple juice and added some grated ginger and orange zest (although I'm not sure the addition of the ginger and zest changed the outcome much.) I did the 400 degrees for 20 minutes, then turned down the oven to 325 for another two hours. I brought the ham interior temp to 140 degrees per the cooking instructions on the ham and it was perfect (it was a fully cooked Martha Stewart bone-in ham from Costco. Almost half the price of the one at the grocery store and I loved it. I would recommend this ham, nothing tasted bargain about it.) I did tent it for the last 45 minutes. When it came out of the oven it looked right out of a magazine, I was very proud to serve this ham to my family. Also, as other reviewers I took the juices from the roasting pan and reduced and served as a sauce. Only thing I would have done different is to skim the reduction before serving. Enjoy!

I made this and thought it was wonderful, but I turned the heat down to 325 degrees after the first 2 hours, and then down to 250 for the last hour and the temperature was right on. I kept the lid on the roaster after the first 20 minutes, and I used cab/shiraz wine. I also allowed it to rest for 1/2 hour before we ate.

First time making holiday ham and it turned out great! Instead of using the whole box of brown sugar, I used light brown sugar and I used about 1/3 of the box. I’m trying to eat healthier. I placed pineapples on the outside of the ham (as shown in the photo) for the last hour. Also I cooked mine in a Dutch over so the presentation of the ham was that of an over cooked appearance but the flavor was still great!

I did not make it home from the store with my jar of whole cloves, so I just sprinkled a little ground cloves over the brown sugar. I used equal amounts of soft rose red wine and pineapple juice then I topped the ham with pineapple and cherries. My ham was a 4.5 pound cooked ham, so I halved the recipe and reduced the cooking time. Everyone loved this. I plan to use this recipe for the Holidays. Thanks for sharing !
Absolutely wonderful.
This recipe is incredible. Prepared as written except for cloves (not my favorite). Devoured to the bone, not even enough left for bean soup. Give it a try!

Wow was this a disaster. Prepared exactly as stated, turned out like beef jerky. It was beyond dry. Something is amiss here. Maybe the ham referred to is fresh not spiral? The recipe is not very clear. I used a spiral and thank God I only paid .69/lb because it was close to inedible. 
Delete this one from the file.
The best ham ever! I mixed ground cloves and the brown sugar…easy and tasted great!
What went wrong? I followed instructions exactly. way too dry. I even tented this.

Full disclosure: I made changes, but not substantial. In the era of Covid, I didn't run out and get more pineapple juice when I only had a cup; I added a can of crushed pineapple. I also had only ground cloves on hand.

Take that as you will, this is an excellent idea, and I had a great outcome.
This was a little bit of work but it came out so tasty! Hubby really liked it and with our Easter lockdown due to COVID-19, lots of leftovers. He’s happy to be having ham sandwiches for lunch.
It was awesome but it didn’t need to cook the full 4 hours. It was falling off the bone in 3 hours
Delicious!
